headline: AI Application Engineering Explained: From LLM APIs to Agents & Production
summary: Go beyond basic LLM integration to build robust AI applications. Learn about context, tools, state management, and production architecture.
details: Integrating a large language model (LLM) into an application is straightforward: send a request, get a response. However, building a reliable AI application involves much more. Real-world applications must manage context, execute tools, preserve state, handle interruptions, request approvals, recover from failures, and communicate progress to users.

This article provides an end-to-end guide to AI application engineering. It covers prompts, context engineering, multimodal AI, tool calling, hooks, approvals, compaction, memory, orchestration, and production architecture. The goal is to understand how these components fit together, the problems they solve, and where each responsibility belongs.

A production AI application can be viewed as several cooperating layers. The provider API exposes model capabilities, while an SDK simplifies its use. A key principle is that the model proposes, the runtime coordinates, tools perform work, and the application enforces policy. This separation is crucial for autonomous AI systems.

Understanding concepts like tokens and context windows is vital. Tokens measure text input, while a context window defines how much information a model can process. However, a larger context window doesn't guarantee better results; irrelevant information can degrade performance.

Modern AI APIs support more than just text. They can handle images, audio, video, documents, structured data, and real-time events. Interactions are often represented as messages with roles, but can include richer content blocks and events, moving beyond simple text-based conversations.

headline_marked: [[Gemini and Chrome]] become a productivity powerhouse
headline: Gemini and Chrome become a productivity powerhouse
summary: Google's AI assistant is now integrated directly into Chrome, streamlining research and task management across multiple tabs and Workspace apps.
details: Google's Gemini AI and Chrome browser have evolved into a potent productivity duo, transforming how users interact with information and manage tasks online.

The 'Ask Gemini' feature places the AI directly within Chrome, eliminating the need to switch between applications. It can summarize web pages, explain complex concepts, and even compare information across multiple open tabs.

This integration extends to Google Workspace apps like Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Drive, Keep, and Tasks. Users can ask Gemini to find emails, check schedules, and suggest meeting times, all without leaving their browser.
The ability to access and synthesize information from up to 10 recent tabs or specific Workspace apps offers a significant advantage for research and planning.
By connecting Gemini with Google Workspace, users can streamline workflows, such as planning a trip by pulling together flight details from Gmail, ideas from Keep, and dates from Calendar.
This seamless integration makes the browser feel more connected and reduces the tedium of manually switching between different tools and applications.
